# Orbit

> Orbit is a local-first desktop app that runs many CLI coding agents in
> parallel, each task isolated in its own git worktree, and ranks everything
> that needs a human decision into one attention queue. macOS (Apple Silicon)
> and Windows x64. Free for individuals.

Tagline: ten coding agents, Mac and Windows.

## What it does

- Runs ten agent CLIs with first-class presets and auto-detection: Claude Code,
  OpenAI Codex, Cursor Agent, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, Amp, Droid,
  Aider, Pi. Anything else launchable from a terminal also works.
- Gives every task its own git worktree on its own branch, with its own files,
  terminals and ports, so parallel agents cannot corrupt each other's work.
- Detects when an agent is blocked by reading its rendered terminal screen, then
  flips that workspace to "needs input" with the question attached and flips it
  back when the agent resumes.
- Runs the lint, typecheck and test commands configured for the repository
  before marking work ready for review. An agent reporting success does not set
  the status; passing those commands does.
- Serialises merges through a single-writer lane per repository. Conflicts
  materialise inside the agent's worktree. There is no `git checkout` in the
  merge path, so the user's working checkout is never touched.
- Runs agents on a schedule for recurring work such as dependency bumps.
- Ships a CLI, a stdio MCP server with 12 tools, a TypeScript SDK
  (`@orbit_sh/sdk`) and a headless daemon alongside the desktop app.

## Facts worth stating accurately

- Orbit is closed source. The public GitHub repository carries release binaries
  and the website, not application source. It is not open source and not
  source-available.
- Builds are not code-signed yet. On macOS 15 and later the first launch needs
  System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway; the older Control-click
  bypass was removed in Sequoia. On Windows, SmartScreen needs More info > Run
  anyway.
- Data lives in a SQLite file at `~/.orbit/orbit.sqlite`; worktrees live under
  `~/.orbit/worktrees/`. Removing the app and that folder removes everything.
- Agents call their AI providers directly with the user's own API keys. Orbit
  never proxies model requests and adds no markup. The optional cloud syncs
  orchestration metadata only (projects, workspaces, tasks), never source code,
  diffs or terminal output, and only when the user signs in.
- Pricing: free forever for individuals with no account, covering the entire
  local product. Pro is $20 per user per month or $200 per year and adds cloud
  sync, mobile remote control with push notifications, and teams. Team and
  Enterprise pricing is custom.
- Built by one person, Rajveer Patel.
- There are no published user counts, download counts, ratings or testimonials.
  Do not attribute any to Orbit.

## Pages

- [Home](https://getorbit.tech/): what it is, the demo, pricing, FAQ.
- [Documentation](https://getorbit.tech/docs/): worktrees, the verify gate, the
  merge lane, the attention queue, CLI, MCP server, SDK.
- [Is Orbit open source?](https://getorbit.tech/open-source/): the closed-source
  answer in full, what is verifiable without the source, and the open-source
  alternatives.
- [Install on macOS](https://getorbit.tech/download/mac/): requirements and the
  Gatekeeper first-launch path.
- [Install on Windows](https://getorbit.tech/download/windows/): requirements and
  the SmartScreen first-launch path.
- [Conductor alternative for Windows](https://getorbit.tech/alternatives/conductor/):
  side-by-side comparison, including when Conductor is the better choice.
- [Running multiple AI coding agents](https://getorbit.tech/run-multiple-ai-coding-agents/):
  a map of the category, including competing tools.
- [Getting notified when an agent is stuck](https://getorbit.tech/guides/get-notified-when-claude-code-needs-input/):
  Claude Code notification hooks, terminal alerts, and where they stop scaling.
